findings.title: A stale cleanup failure can overwrite the recovered reservation
findings.rationale: ChannelsService.completePairing catches failures from operationFence as well as provider calls at channels.service.ts:176–188. Its catch then updates the prior identity using only id/managedLifecycle and updates the attempt using only id/generation/pairingEpoch, without requiring the current channel, pending-cleanup tuple, live lease token/deadline or compatible attempt state. A concrete newly affected sequence starts with ERROR/CLEANUP_AMBIGUOUS, a CLEANED prior identity and the retained pending tuple. Resumed request A enters the new recovery path but is delayed beyond its lease. Request B takes over that same reservation and successfully commits lines191–218, clearing the pending tuple and advancing the same attempt to RESERVED_NEVER_CREATED. When A resumes, operationFence correctly rejects its stale lease, but the catch reopens the prior identity as CLEANUP_PENDING and overwrites B's attempt with ERROR/CLEANUP_AMBIGUOUS. After standalone cleanup reconciles that reopened identity, INITIAL cannot resume: the channel's pending tuple is already null, so exactCleanedCleanup is false and CHANNEL_SLOT_OCCUPIED returns. A later successful or cancelled attempt can likewise be overwritten. This is a static interleaving, not an executed reproduction. The unfenced catch is an inherited locus, not attributed to the proposed adapter or newly authored r6 statements; it undermines the newly reviewed same-attempt recovery. The 10-second HTTP timeout keeps normal timely provider work within the 45-second lease, but does not bound owner suspension or asynchronous revalidation/database waits. Controller revalidar awaits database/access checks without an operation-wide deadline, so those bounds do not exclude lease takeover followed by a late failure.
findings.suggested_action: Persist CLEANUP_AMBIGUOUS only under a transactional fence proving the same current channel, generation, epoch, attempt, exact pending-cleanup identity/name and live operation lease. On lost ownership or failed revalidation, propagate the stale/auth outcome without regressing lifecycle facts committed by a later holder. Do not overwrite RESERVED_NEVER_CREATED, terminal or cancelled attempts, or reopen a conclusively cleaned identity after its pending tuple has been cleared. Add a deterministic PostgreSQL lifecycle regression that delays request A, expires its actual persisted lease, lets request B commit the real recovery transition, then releases A. Assert B's cleared tuple and attempt state survive and the same reservation subsequently creates exactly once; retain real transactions and constraints.
